lessons.concept: A weight is one number in a matrix that scales a signal.
lessons.eli5: A weight is a volume knob on one wire. Programming weights means turning knobs on purpose instead of hoping.
lessons.title: What is a weight?

lessons.concept: A forward pass is dot products between rows of weights and an activation vector.
lessons.eli5: Each output is a shopping receipt: multiply what came in by each price, then add it all up.
lessons.title: Weights times activations, by hand

lessons.concept: Training nudges weights opposite the gradient of a loss.
lessons.eli5: Gradient descent is walking downhill in fog: feel the slope under one foot, take a small step.
lessons.title: Loss, gradients, and why weights move

lessons.concept: A layer is a named block of weights with a fixed shape.
lessons.eli5: A layer is a shelf in a warehouse: one address, many boxes.
lessons.title: Layers as weight blocks

lessons.concept: Attention routes information from sets of positions to sets of positions, which is an ultra-edge.
lessons.eli5: A neighborhood mail route delivers to a whole street at once, not one house.
lessons.title: Attention heads as ultra-edges

lessons.concept: Distances between embedding rows encode similarity.
lessons.eli5: Words are cities on a map; similar meanings sit closer together.
lessons.title: Geometry of embedding weights

lessons.concept: Sparsity trades capacity for generalization; measure both.
lessons.eli5: A backpack with fewer tools is easier to carry, as long as you keep the ones you need.
lessons.title: More weights is not better

lessons.concept: Token ids index embedding rows; weights are selected by data.
lessons.eli5: Tokens are page numbers; the embedding table is the book.
lessons.title: From bytes to tokens

lessons.concept: Each head owns a slice of the projection weights.
lessons.eli5: A head is one reader in a study group, each skimming a different chapter.
lessons.title: Attention heads in a tiny model

lessons.concept: Routing selects expert blocks; the selection pattern is a directed graph.
lessons.eli5: A hospital receptionist sends you to the right specialist, not all of them.
lessons.title: Mixture of experts as routing edges

lessons.concept: Context changes activations, not weights; the two must not be confused.
lessons.eli5: Weights are the recipe, context is the ingredients you happen to have.
lessons.title: How weights shape context

lessons.concept: Each weight becomes -1, 0, or +1; two bits per value.
lessons.eli5: Dimmer switches become light switches: dim, off, bright. Cheaper and much faster.
lessons.title: Ternary weights: the light-switch model

lessons.concept: A threshold decides the trit; a per-group scale restores magnitude.
lessons.eli5: Round the pennies for the pocket, keep the dollars for the bank.
lessons.title: Thresholds and scales

lessons.concept: Pruning removes coordinates and edges while preserving invariants.
lessons.eli5: Cutting roads only helps if the towns you care about stay connected.
lessons.title: Sparsity and ultra-edge cuts

lessons.concept: A diff is a reversible edit set bound to a base snapshot identity.
lessons.eli5: Keep the receipt, not the whole grocery store; you can always reconstruct the trip.
lessons.title: Versioning weights with receipts

lessons.concept: Inference reads weights and writes activations; ternary kernels trade accuracy for speed.
lessons.eli5: Cooking dinner uses the recipe and the pantry; you do not rewrite the recipe each time.
lessons.title: What happens at query time

lessons.concept: Agents drive the same operations through MCP tools, so results are identical.
lessons.eli5: A robot arm using your own tools is still your workshop.
lessons.title: Let an agent program your weights
